atoms.a:
Sarina picks 12 ripe apples with her Grandma.
On average, one apple weighs 110 g.

How much do the apples weigh all together?

atoms.b: The apples weigh <mat><gap>1320</gap></mat> g or <mat><gap>1.32</gap></mat> kg.

atoms.a:
Miriam has a dog. The dog eats 2 kg of food per day.

How much does the dog eat in one week?

atoms.b: The dog eats <mat><gap>14</gap></mat> kg in a week.

atoms.a:
Bruno is a baker and has prepared 15 kg of dough.
If each loaf uses 500 g of dough, how many loaves of bread can he bake?

atoms.b: Bruno can make <mat><gap>30</gap></mat> loaves of bread.

atoms.a: Bruno accidentally burns 6 loaves of bread. How many kilograms of dough has been wasted?

atoms.b: <mat><gap>3</gap></mat> kg of dough has been wasted.

atoms.a:
The Miller family’s book collection weighs 100 kg in total. One bookshelf can hold 20 kg.

How many bookshelves will the family need to buy, so they can put all of their books on the shelves?

Mr Miller is going to carry the shelves home from the shop. Each shelf weighs 15.5 kg and Mr Miller can comfortably carry up to 78 kg.

Will the shelves be too heavy for Mr Miller to carry comfortably?

atoms.b: Mr Miller ((++can cannot)) carry the shelves comfortably.
